en.title: Global growth is holding up, but industrial output is diverging
en.deck: October crude-steel output fell 1.1% across 70 reporting economies, but regional production and business sentiment diverged; Germany’s improving climate, weaker manufacturing confidence and the US equity reversal show why aggregate growth headlines are incomplete.
en.regime: Global activity remains expansionary in several major economies, but industrial output, business sentiment and financing conditions differ sharply by region and sector.
en.key_risk: A wider regional industrial slowdown combined with higher credit premia and renewed energy-logistics disruption could weaken investment and employment before aggregate global GDP turns negative.

signal_rationale.delta: The 23 November edition examined China's iron-ore/steel chain and exporter inventories. This edition retains a distinct cross-region activity and financing thesis but adds the newly released October global crude-steel data and Germany's November Ifo survey, then updates the market and oil session reported on 24 November. The new evidence shows regional industrial divergence rather than a synchronized collapse.
signal_rationale.evidence: Worldsteel reported 142.4 Mt crude-steel output in October across 70 economies, down 1.1% y/y; Jan-Oct output was down 0.8%. North America rose 5.6%, Africa 7.9%, the EU fell 4.0%, the Middle East 27.7%, South America 4.1%, and Asia/Oceania was flat. Germany's Ifo climate index rose to 90.6, but manufacturing confidence fell. Reuters reported Nasdaq -1.4%, S&P 500 -0.50%, Dow +0.85%, Brent +2.27% to US$91.40 and a 0.44% dollar decline in its 24 November session report. Existing PMI, high-yield spread, IIF portfolio-flow and Brazil macrofiscal observations retain their original vintages.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Regional steel production and survey dispersion affect expectations for industrial orders, employment, inventories and trade; these differences shape central-bank decisions, sovereign yields and currency conditions; credit premia and cross-border flows then affect investment, while oil, refined products and shipping transmit geopolitical risk into delivered costs.
signal_rationale.transmission: Regional activity and steel output -> sector revenue, employment and inventories -> domestic inflation and monetary policy -> yields, FX and refinancing costs -> portfolio flows and investment. Oil supply and shipping reports -> crude and refined-product prices -> transport and industrial costs -> inflation expectations and policy response.
signal_rationale.falsifier: The thesis weakens if subsequent national accounts and industrial-production releases show broad, synchronized acceleration, regional steel-output gaps narrow, the Germany-France survey divergence closes, high-yield spreads reverse their November widening, non-resident EM portfolio flows return to positive territory and refined-product premiums decline.

key_constraints: Flash PMIs and the Ifo business-climate index are surveys, not GDP growth rates or measured industrial output.

Worldsteel's 70 reporting economies represented about 98% of global crude-steel output in 2025; US and Russian monthly output are estimates. Steel production is not a direct measure of final demand, inventories or trade.
The October steel figures are one month of sector output; year-to-date changes and country-level product mixes differ.
The US high-yield OAS series ends on 20 November and is not a 24 November market close; it covers US dollar below-investment-grade bonds, not all credit.
IIF portfolio flows are October monthly estimates, not daily November flows.
The Brazil Ministry of Finance parameter grid was closed on 6 November; it is a forecast vintage, not a realised outcome or market-consensus survey.
FAO's food-price index is an international commodity basket, not a retail-price or household-affordability measure; the latest meat component mixes projected and observed prices and can be revised.
Reports of vessel attacks around the Strait of Hormuz are attributed to Reuters reporting; the available material does not quantify a sustained loss of oil output or exports.
The US Treasury curve and the 24 November Reuters yield observation refer to different dates and should not be merged into a single curve.
The 23 November Brazil Focus medians are market expectations for 2026, not Central Bank forecasts, and are distinct from the Ministry of Finance's 2027 parameter grid.

producer_checks.novelty_decision: Revision 7 adds newly released October global steel output and the 24 November German Ifo survey to the cross-region activity and financing-dispersion thesis. It does not repeat the 23 November China iron-ore/steel-inventory article.

reproducibility_notes.pmi_comparison: Flash composite PMI output indices published 23–24 Nov 2026; 50 is the expansion/contraction threshold. The values are survey diffusion indices, not GDP growth rates.
reproducibility_notes.credit_spread: ICE BofA US High Yield Index OAS via FRED, unit Percent: 3.23% on 13 Nov; 3.34% on 16 Nov; 3.43% on 17 Nov; 3.47% on 18 Nov; 3.52% on 19 Nov; 3.76% on 20 Nov. Latest observation available at the 05:00 BRT cutoff.
reproducibility_notes.treasury_curve: US Treasury official daily par curve, 23 Nov 2026: 2-year 4.63%; 10-year 4.92%; 30-year 5.29%.
reproducibility_notes.brazil_forecast: Brazil Ministry of Finance November 2026 Macrofiscal Bulletin, summary p.3 and detailed grid discussion p.19; grid closed 6 Nov. For 2027, GDP 1.8% (September 2.3%), IPCA 4.5% (3.8%), accumulated Selic 12.93% (12.67%), average exchange rate R$5.34/US$ (R$5.23), and average Brent US$95.20/bbl (US$79.50). The grid's Selic is derived from the real rate implicit in the Focus median (nominal Selic adjusted for market inflation expectations) and converted to nominal terms with the SPE inflation projection; it is distinct from the Focus terminal Selic median of 12.75% at end-2027. FX and Brent are annual averages, not terminal or spot prices.
reproducibility_notes.oil_market: Reuters settlement values for 23 Nov; IEA November report supplies October production and inventory estimates. Spot/futures settlement and monthly supply estimates are different observation types.
reproducibility_notes.food_prices: FAO October 2026 FFPI: 133.9, down 1.2% m/m; cereal 116.8, down 4.5%; sugar 121.3, up 6.6%.
reproducibility_notes.market_flows: IIF tracker published 5 Nov, estimating October non-resident EM portfolio outflows of US$33.8bn; monthly estimate, not daily flow.
reproducibility_notes.brazil_focus: Banco Central do Brasil Focus report with reference date 19 Nov 2026, summarized by B3 on 23 Nov: 2026 GDP 1.70% (from 1.72%), IPCA 5.15% (from 5.11%), and year-end USD/BRL 5.55 (from 5.40). These are market medians, not Central Bank forecasts, and are distinct from the Ministry of Finance's 2027 parameter grid. Primary PDF: https://www.bcb.gov.br/content/focus/focus/R20261119.pdf.
reproducibility_notes.japan_policy: Bank of Japan policy decision published 18 Sep 2026 sets the uncollateralized overnight call-rate guideline around 1.25% and states that the change applies from the next business day, 24 Sep; the October 2026 Outlook Report confirms the level.
reproducibility_notes.brazil_ptax: Banco Central do Brasil PTAX OData historical query for 23 Nov 2026: selling rate 5.97080 at 13:06:23 BRT; date-filtered endpoint retained for reproducibility.
reproducibility_notes.worldsteel_production: World Steel Association, October 2026 release published 24 Nov 2026. Production for 70 reporting countries was 142.4 Mt (-1.1% y/y); Jan-Oct was 1,509.3 Mt (-0.8%). October regional changes: Africa +7.9%, Asia/Oceania 0.0%, EU -4.0%, Europe other +5.1%, Middle East -27.7%, North America +5.6%, Russia/CIS/Ukraine -6.8%, South America -4.1%. The 70 countries represented approximately 98% of 2025 world production. US and Russian country figures are estimates.
reproducibility_notes.ifo_november: ifo Institute press release 24 Nov 2026: Business Climate 90.6 (Oct 90.1); current conditions 89.4 (88.8); expectations 91.9 (91.5). Aggregate sentiment improved, but manufacturing weakened after six increases and expectations returned to negative territory; services and trade improved and construction slipped.
reproducibility_notes.reuters_markets_24nov: Reuters report dated 24 Nov 2026: Nasdaq -1.4%, S&P 500 -0.50%, Dow +0.85%; Nvidia shares >6% lower after prior session's +31.5%; dollar -0.44%; US 10-year yield 4.928% vs 4.92% late Monday; Brent January futures settled US$91.40/bbl, +US$2.03 or 2.27%, amid reported vessel attacks around Hormuz. Attribute incident reports and do not infer sustained physical output losses.
